title: Spreading a prescribed stable valuation model to a quasi-alteration
statement: Let $T$ be an integral scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], let $L$ be a separable closure of $k(T)$, and let $x\in RZ_L(T)$ correspond to $V$ as in [lem-trf-riemann-zariski-finite-refinement]. Let $(X,D)$ be a multipointed $T$-curve with smooth generic curve and etale generic marking. Suppose a stable $\eta$-modification of $(X,D)\times_T\operatorname{Spec}V$ has been specified. Then there exists an $L$-quasi-model $U\to T$, a lift $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U$, and a stable $\eta$-modification $(Y,E)\to(X,D)\times_T U$ over the integral scheme $U$ whose pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}V$ is isomorphic to the specified modification; moreover there is a dense open $U^\circ\subseteq U$ such that both the curve map and the marking map are isomorphisms over the preimages of $U^\circ$, which contain the generic fibres. The open $RZ_L(U)$ contains $x$. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Finite type for scheme morphisms has the meaning of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.
